newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils close with muted reaction to Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils close with muted reaction to Chicago.

text.p: European vegetable oil sellers were not falling over themselves to mark down prices at the close following the sharply lower opening in Chicago on Monday.
"We've seen Chicago bounce back on the slightness pretext too often when the weather market is running, so most people will wait until Tuesday before making a move," said a trader.
Palm oil prices have been under pressure for most of the day following bearish data release by PORLA and MOPGC.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) put local end-August stocks at 800,893 tonnes against 755,665 at end July.
Palm oil output was put at 810,550 tonnes up 12.21 percent from July, while exports were 638,601 tonnes against 662,035 tonnes the previous month.
The Malaysian Oil Palm Growers' Council (MOPGC) also released an estimate which put local palm oil output in August at 825,000 tonnes, 14.3 percent up from July.

However, Malaysian cargo surveyor, Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) released figures which put Malaysian exports during the first 15 days of September at 310,058 tonnes against 287,394 tonnes during the same period in August.
Traders said lower palm oil prices could attract buyers and they did not rule out tenders from India before its harvest starts if prices continue to fall.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $5.00 down in a tradeless market while refined palm oils were $5.00 to $12.50 a tonne lower with no further business reported during the afternoon.
Lauric oils attracted some light trade with Sep/Oct coconut oil fetching $732.50 and $730.00/tonne and $712.50 was paid for Sep/Oct palmkernel oil. Closing sellers were around $2.50 lower.
Dutch soy oil closed unchanged while rape oil was 0.50 guilders down after Sep traded at 98.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill. -- Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
